transcript.content: Hello. Welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel constantly wound up and on edge, like I can’t relax even when I’m just at home with my family. It has gotten to the point where I'm always tense, and my wife urged me to come in and get some help.
How long have you been feeling this constant tension and inability to relax?

It's been going on for about nine months now. It really started ramping up around the time my wife went back to work full-time and I took on a massive cloud migration project at my job. Since then, it just feels like I haven't been able to catch my breath.
Besides your work project and your family's schedule, do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different everyday things, and is it difficult to control or stop these worries?

Yes, absolutely. I worry about everything from my kids getting sick to my parents' health, and even simple decisions like planning dinner snowball in my head. It's incredibly hard to stop because my mind just chains these "what-if" worst-case scenarios together, and I can't shut it off even when I'm on the floor playing with my kids.
Along with this constant worry, have you also been experiencing symptoms like trouble sleeping, feeling easily irritated, or having difficulty concentrating?

Yes, all of those are taking a huge toll. I lie awake for hours replaying schedules and wake up at 3 or 4 a.m. stressing about work and finances, which makes me so exhausted that I zone out in meetings and constantly lose my train of thought. It's also made me really irritable, and I find myself snapping at my wife and withdrawing from the family because I'm just so completely drained.

Are you currently taking any medications, using substances like caffeine or alcohol excessively, or do you have any medical conditions like thyroid issues that might be contributing to these feelings?

No, I'm not taking any medications, and I don't have any medical conditions like thyroid issues as far as I know. I also don't drink much alcohol or caffeine; when I described feeling like I've had too much coffee, I just meant that's how the physical tension feels. I'm otherwise physically healthy.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with excessive anxiety and worry about a variety of everyday events (family health, simple decisions, work, finances) that has persisted for 9 months, meeting the duration criterion of at least 6 months. The worry is difficult to control and is accompanied by several physical and cognitive symptoms including muscle tension, sleep disturbance (difficulty falling and staying asleep), irritability, difficulty concentrating, and fatigue. These symptoms cause significant distress and functional impairment in his family and work life, and are not attributable to substances or a general medical condition, confirming a diagnosis of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1).
